analysis: What changed versus the 5:00 AM brief: the overnight uncertainty resolved in the worst direction — Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO, effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and board member Harvey Jones as the company's first chairman. NVDA deepened its premarket slide to -10.4% ($155.68, Finnhub 8:59 AM ET) from -7.5% at 5:00 AM. The resignation converts a governance overhang into a leadership vacuum five days before Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings: Huang co-founded the company in 1993, has said he does not believe in succession planning, and there is no named permanent successor. The chip split hardened: AMD +3.9% on a William Blair upgrade and Broadcom +1.9% as rotation beneficiaries, while Nvidia-funded names (Intel, Marvell, Micron, CoreWeave -10%) fell harder. Nebius also slid further, to about -15% premarket, as the earnings call put numbers on the funding question — 2027 capex of $40-45B against $12-13B of revenue, with the Microsoft New Jersey build slipping to 2Q27. The one offset: Reuters' Morning Bid notes the market has removed the small chance of a 50bp December Fed hike overnight, back to a quarter-point. Jobless claims (200K vs 195K expected) are slightly soft but are not moving anything next to Nvidia. Signal vs noise: the resignation is confirmed by the company via Reuters and WSJ — signal, and the day's dominant one; the HN thread on the WSJ ouster report (1,545 comments) now reads as the prelude; Polymarket/Kalshi odds and Musk's 'honor to hire' comment are noise.

community_signals.takeaway: 1,545-comment thread on the WSJ report that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust Huang — posted hours before the resignation landed, it is now the best record of how the community read the governance risk, the succession vacuum, and the circular-financing exposure before the news broke.
community_signals.title: Nvidia is preparing to oust Jensen Huang

disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned, the company said Thursday; CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO and board member Harvey Jones — former Synopsys CEO — becomes Nvidia's first-ever board chairman. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and owns about 3.61%, will exit the board as well. NVDA fell more than 10% premarket to $155.68 (-10.39% vs Wednesday's $173.73 close, Finnhub 8:59 AM ET). The board met Wednesday night after the NYT reported a second affair, with Nvidia healthcare VP Kimberly Powell, who reports to Huang; the first involved a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Huang has said he does not believe in succession planning and never named a successor.
headlines.why_it_matters: The overnight uncertainty resolved in the worst direction — a leadership vacuum, not a conduct probe, five days before Nov 17 earnings, and the -10% move prices the loss of the AI trade's central figure, not a demand problem.

headlines.headline: Bernstein cut its Nvidia price target to $200 from $400 and Morgan Stanley dropped NVDA from its top-pick list (CNBC). One analyst estimate cited by Bloomberg put Nvidia's fair value without Huang at about $225 a share, against $300 if he stays.
headlines.why_it_matters: Wall Street is now pricing a 'Huang discount' into the stock itself — the downgrades frame the move as a valuation reset on leadership, not a one-day headline dip.

headlines.headline: Nebius (NBIS) slid to about -15% premarket (~$131) after the Q3 beat, deepening from -8.3% at 5:00 AM as the earnings call detailed the funding plan: 2027 revenue guidance of $12-13B against 2027 capex of $40-45B, with the Microsoft New Jersey build slipping to 2Q27 and December revenue slipping to February, pushing 2026 revenue to the low end of $3.0-3.4B. Q3 revenue was $980.8M (+571% YoY) vs ~$907M expected, adjusted EPS -$0.13 vs -$0.72 expected, adjusted EBITDA $465.8M (47% margin), and ARR at end-September was $6.4B. NBIS closed Wednesday at $154.69 (+15.44%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat is now fully overshadowed by the bill — $40-45B of 2027 capex against $12-13B of revenue keeps the funding question, not demand, as the swing factor for the neoclouds.

SPY traded $756.39 (-0.45%) and QQQ $684.02 (-0.92%) premarket at 7:05 AM ET. The prior session (Wed Nov 11) closed strong: S&P 500 +1.31% to 7,619.38, Nasdaq Composite +1.60% to 25,466.19, Dow +0.5% (~+255 pts). Note: the 8:44 AM ET futures snapshot predates the Reuters resignation report; NVDA's slide deepened after it.
headlines.why_it_matters: Wednesday's CoreWeave-led rally is giving back its tech half overnight, with the Nasdaq taking roughly twice the S&P's damage — the selling is concentrated in AI names, not broad-based.

headlines.headline: The chip split hardened overnight: AMD rose 3.9% after William Blair upgraded it to Outperform from Market Perform, and Broadcom gained ~1.9% premarket ($351.82, Finnhub 8:59 AM ET). On the other side, CoreWeave fell ~10% to $54.33, Intel fell ~2.6-3.4%, Marvell ~2.8-3.9%, and Micron ~2.6-3.4%; optical suppliers Coherent and Lumentum fell ~4-5%. Alibaba fell as much as 7.1% in Hong Kong on worries over Chinese cloud operators' access to advanced chips.
headlines.why_it_matters: Traders are rotating within AI, not out of it — rivals gain on share-gain hopes while Nvidia-funded names fall on funding fears, so the open is a stock-picking tape, not a sector rout.

headlines.headline: Initial jobless claims rose to 200,000 for the week ending Nov 7, above the ~195,000 expected and the prior week's 191,000 (revised from 189,000), per the Labor Department. The 4-week moving average held at 195,250. Continuing claims fell 20,000 to 1.697M, below the 1.710M expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: Slightly softer than expected but not market-moving next to Nvidia — a modest loosening read that sits oddly beside the Deutsche Bank three-hike call and does not change the rates debate today.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The fresh angle is crude firming: WTI $86.80 (+0.31%) after Wednesday's +1.21% rebound, which keeps the energy tailwind from yesterday intact. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M, and the J-W Power acquisition closed (~$860M, adding 0.8M+ horsepower for a combined fleet of ~4.4M, ~5M at quarter end). RBC raised its price target to $31 from $30 (Nov 7). Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.

watch_next: Nvidia's search for a permanent CEO — who is floated, and whether the board moves fast or leaves Kress as interim through the Nov 17 earnings print; the requested House briefing is Nov 18 and its status post-resignation is unclear.
